exact_snippets: ([[thm-minus-laplacian-of-the-fundamental-solution-is-dirac]] for the first identity, [[lem-em-distributional-gradient-smooth-off-a-point]] for the passage from the potential to the field, [[def-distributional-derivative]], [[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]).

3.1 Coulomb representation: since Lebesgue measure is translation invariant, $N\rho(x)=\int\Phi(x-y)\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y)=\int\Phi(z)\rho(x-z)\,d\lambda_3(z)$ ([F6]); fix $i\in\{1,2,3\}$, $x_0\in\mathbb R^3$, $\delta>0$ and the interval $J=(-\delta,\delta)$ of coordinate increments, so $x_0+se_i\in B(x_0,\delta)$ for $s\in J$. For such $x$ the integrand $\Phi(z)\rho(x-z)$ is supported in the compact ball $K:=\overline B_{|x_0|+\delta+R}(0)$, and its $s$-derivative $\Phi(z)\partial_i\rho(x-z)$ is dominated on $J$ by $\|\nabla\rho\|_\infty|\Phi(z)|\mathbf 1_K(z)$, which is integrable ([F5], [F8]); differentiation under the integral sign [F6] therefore gives $\partial_iN\rho(x)=\int\Phi(z)\partial_i\rho(x-z)\,d\lambda_3(z)$. For fixed $x$ put $h(z):=\rho(x-z)$, a $C^1$ compactly supported function; then $\partial_i\rho(x-z)=-\partial_{z_i}h(z)$, so $$\partial_iN\rho(x)=-\int\Phi(z)\partial_{z_i}h(z)\,d\lambda_3(z).$$ The kernel $\Phi$ is locally integrable, continuous and smooth off the single point $0$, its classical partials are locally integrable, so [[lem-em-distributional-gradient-smooth-off-a-point]] applies with $u=\Phi$ and gives $\partial_iT_\Phi=T_{\partial_i\Phi}$; This identity is initially paired only with smooth tests: for $h_\delta$ of [F11], $\int\Phi\partial_i h_\delta=-\int\partial_i\Phi\,h_\delta$ by [F7]. Since $h\in C_c^1$, [F11] supplies uniform convergence of both $h_\delta$ and $\partial_i h_\delta$ on a fixed compact support; the two locally integrable kernels therefore allow the limit $\int\Phi\partial_i h=-\int\partial_i\Phi\,h$, without pairing any distribution against a nonsmooth test. Substituting back and translating gives $$\partial_iN\rho(x)=\int\partial_i\Phi(x-y)\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y)=-\frac{1}{4\pi}\int\frac{x_i-y_i}{|x-y|^3}\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y)$$ for every $x\in\mathbb R^3$, the integral being absolutely convergent because $\operatorname{supp}\rho\subseteq\overline B_R$ lies in the ball $B(x,|x|+2R)$ and $\int_{B(x,|x|+2R)}|x-y|^{-2}d\lambda_3(y)=4\pi(|x|+2R)<\infty$, while $|\rho|\le\|\rho\|_\infty$ on the support ([F1], [F5], [F8]). Multiplying by $-\varepsilon_0^{-1}$ gives exactly the displayed Coulomb representation of $E=-\nabla\varphi$. [step 2.1, F1, F5, F6, F7, F8, F11]

8.1 Clause (d), field identities and reading: by [[lem-em-distributional-gradient-smooth-off-a-point]] applied to $u=\varphi_q$ (locally integrable, continuous and smooth off the single point $x_0$, classical partials locally integrable), $\partial_iT_{\varphi_q}=T_{\partial_i\varphi_q}$ ([F7]). Since $E_{q,i}=-\partial_i\varphi_q$ off $x_0$ and a singleton is null, the two functions agree almost everywhere, hence $T_{E_{q,i}}=-T_{\partial_i\varphi_q}=-\partial_iT_{\varphi_q}$ ([F7]); taking one more distributional derivative and summing over $i$ gives $$\operatorname{div}E_q=\sum_i\partial_iT_{E_{q,i}}=-\sum_i\partial_i\partial_iT_{\varphi_q}=-\Delta T_{\varphi_q}=\frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}\delta_{x_0},$$ and the curl components vanish because distributional partial derivatives commute: $$\partial_2T_{E_{q,3}}-\partial_3T_{E_{q,2}}=-(\partial_2\partial_3-\partial_3\partial_2)T_{\varphi_q}=0,$$ and likewise for the other two components ([F7]). By [F9] the distribution $q\delta_{x_0}$ is the fixed-time reading of the stationary point source with charge $q$ at $x_0$, so $(E_q,0)$ satisfies the distributional pure electrostatic equations with that source. No product of distributions was formed, no value of the field at $x_0$ was used, and no uniqueness, self-force, reaction or empirical claim is made; this is exactly the scope stated. [step 7.1, F7, F8, F9] ∎

exact_snippets: Assume the Axiom of Choice for the cited Sobolev trace/weak-solvability interfaces and Countable Choice for the surface-measure interfaces ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $B:=B_1(0)=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:|x|<1\}$ be the open unit ball, a bounded $C^\infty$ (in particular $C^1$) domain with $\partial B=S^2$ and outward normal $\nu(x)=x$ ([[lem-em-euclidean-balls-and-annuli-are-bounded-c-one-domains]], [[def-metric-ball]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]), and consider the pure electrostatic Neumann problem on $B$ (regime [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]], fields [[def-em-fields]], constants [[def-em-si-conventions]]) with **zero volume source and unit outward normal derivative**:

[F2] The unit ball is a bounded $C^\infty$ domain (in particular a bounded $C^1$ domain) with $\partial B=S^2$, outward normal $\nu(x)=x$ on $S^2$, a compact embedded $C^\infty$ hypersurface carrying its finite surface measure; moreover $|S^{n-1}|=n|B_1|$, and with $V_3(1)=\pi^{3/2}/\Gamma(5/2)$, $\Gamma(5/2)=\frac32\cdot\frac12\,\Gamma(1/2)=\frac{3\sqrt\pi}{4}$ and $\Gamma(1/2)=\sqrt\pi$, one computes $V_3(1)=4\pi/3$ and $|S^2|=3\cdot4\pi/3=4\pi$ ([[lem-em-euclidean-balls-and-annuli-are-bounded-c-one-domains]], [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]], [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]], [[thm-real-gamma-functional-equation]], [[cor-real-gamma-one-half-is-root-pi]], [[def-metric-ball]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]).

exact_snippets: [F2] Green's first identity holds on a bounded $C^1$ domain for real $u=v\in C^2$ up to the closure, with the outward normal; the Euclidean balls are bounded $C^1$ domains with outward normal $x/|x|$ on their bounding spheres, and $|S_{R'}|=4\pi R'^2$ ([[cor-first-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]], [[lem-em-euclidean-balls-and-annuli-are-bounded-c-one-domains]], [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]], [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]]).

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the cited Lebesgue, spherical-harmonic and Newtonian interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $a>0$ and let $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ be real and vanish $\lambda_3$-a.e. outside $\overline B_a(0)$ ([[def-metric-ball]], [[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]); let $Q$, $p$ and $Q_{ij}$ be the total charge, dipole moment and traceless quadrupole of $\rho$ about the chart origin ([[def-em-electric-moments]] (a)); let $\varphi:=\varepsilon_0^{-1}N\rho$ be the potential of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]] (c) with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]] ([[def-newtonian-potential]]); and let $\{Y_{lm}:l\ge0,\ m=1,\dots,2l+1\}$ be a real orthonormal basis of spherical harmonics of $L^2(S^2,d\sigma)$ of degree $l$, with $d\sigma$ the surface measure of total mass $4\pi$ and the addition theorem of [[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]] ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). For every $l,m$ define the **spherical multipole moment of degree $l$**

[F3] In dimension three the fundamental solution is $\Phi(z)=1/(4\pi|z|)$ away from the pole; for compactly supported real $L^1$ data $\rho$ the potential $N\rho$ is finite $\lambda_3$-a.e., locally integrable, $C^\infty$ and harmonic off the support, and $-\Delta T_{\varepsilon_0^{-1}N\rho}=T_{\rho/\varepsilon_0}$ in $\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$ ([[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]]).

exact_snippets: (b) [Undefined self-interaction; nonzero and zero source branches] The framework's source model [[def-em-weak-sources]] pairs distributions against compact smooth tests and expressly excludes arbitrary products of distributions. An explicit nonzero singular self-field is the stationary Coulomb field of [[pthm-em-coulomb-solution]](d): for a constant trajectory $z(t)=x_0$ and $q\ne0$, $|E_q(x)|=|q|/(4\pi\varepsilon_0|x-x_0|^2)$ for $x\ne x_0$, which tends to infinity as $x\to x_0$. Its point-source charge distribution is supported on that stationary worldline. For $q=0$, the point-source pairings of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) give $\rho_{\mathrm{pt}}=J_{\mathrm{pt}}=0$ for every admitted trajectory; in the stationary Coulomb source-field branch, $E_q=0$ off $x_0$ extends smoothly by zero, with $B=0$. Thus that zero-source branch has no self-field singularity and no nontrivial self-interaction. This states the source-field branch, not uniqueness among fields with an additional free field.
